metric_name: Fatalities at managed operations; All-injury frequency rate; Potential fatal incidents
context_text: The safety and wellbeing of our employees, contractors and communities is core to our values, and to what we stand for as a company. Nothing matters more.；Tragically, in August 2025, our colleague Mohamed Camara was fatally injured while changing a heavy mobile equipment tyre at the SimFer mine site in Guinea.；We recorded 87 potential fatal incidents (PFIs) during the year.；Fatalities at managed operations 1 (2024: 5 fatalities).；All-injury frequency rate (AIFR) at 0.37 (target: 0.38). (2024: 0.37).
label: Suspected Greenwash
llm_reason: The claim’s decisive assertion is that safety and wellbeing are the company’s top priority (“core to our values… Nothing matters more”). The provided evidence only lists safety-related metrics and values (1 fatality at managed operations; all-injury frequency rate 0.37 per 200,000 hours worked; 87 potential fatal incidents) but does not substantiate the asserted priority/value ranking, nor demonstrate that safety and wellbeing are treated as the highest priority in practice. The presence of 1 fatality and 87 potential fatal incidents also does not verify the implied outcome-oriented message that safety is effectively protected. No evidence is provided about policies, governance, actions, targets, or comparative prioritization to support the claim as written.
